National Assembly
Twenty-ninth Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
Magh 23, 2082 - Friday
Meeting Number: 17
The meeting commenced today at 13:19 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson of the National Assembly, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson: The proceedings of the National Assembly meeting commence now. Honourable members, time has been allocated for Honourable Members to speak during the Zero Hour. Each Honourable Member has been allocated one minute to speak. First, Honourable Member Ganga Kumari Belbase.

Honourable Ms. Ganga Kumari Belbase (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
Honourable Chairperson, news has come that medicines are not available in hospitals, and health insurance is not being provided. Hospitals respond that treatment cannot be provided under health insurance, and ministers are meeting to secure funds from the government. The current situation of health insurance is dire, and there is a problem. This is a public welfare program, and patients are left stranded without treatment. This hospital is in such a state. It needs to be run smoothly, managed scientifically, and a system should be implemented where those who can afford it pay and those who cannot receive subsidies. I conclude my remarks. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Tulasa Kumari Dahal.

Honourable Ms. Tulasa Kumari Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, there are reports of a new virus entering India. Due to our open border, it could enter Nepal. I request the Ministry of Health to provide information on the arrangements being made at the borders for management. Similarly, regarding health insurance, which is a subject that the general public has been benefiting from and utilizing, there are reports that hospitals and some government bodies have stopped services citing non-payment of funds by the government. It is also heard that the Honourable Prime Minister has taken interest in this matter. I also request information on what has been done for its management.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Dr. Beduram Bhusal.

Honourable Dr. Beduram Bhusal (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):- Honourable Chairperson, Section 3 of the Departmental Act, 2081, mandates that the government must list bills in priority order and present them to the parliament by the end of Ashad. Accordingly, for this year, the government had informed the parliament that it would introduce 121 bills: 42 bills in the first priority, 41 bills in the second priority, and 38 bills in the third priority. I have the list of these 121 bills. I request the government to inform this parliament about the status of draft preparation for these bills. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Maya Prasad Sharma.

Honourable Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):- Honourable Chairperson, regarding the security of old heritage properties within the old Parliament building, it was stated that reconstruction work should be carried out with vigilance for their security. What is the status of that? Furthermore, the new Parliament building was supposed to be constructed and handed over by Push 16, 2082. Has that building been constructed? What is its status? When will it be handed over? Will it be ready by Push 16? I wish to draw the government's attention to this through the Honourable Chairperson. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Sumitra B.C.

Honourable Ms. Sumitra B.C (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, through you, I want to ask the government: this government was established with the objective of holding elections within six months. Its statements sometimes suggest a two-phase election, and sometimes that it might be delayed. Since the Prime Minister himself has made such statements, I demand that the government hold a fair, transparent, and fear-free election promptly and simultaneously. I also request a guarantee of security in areas where there is currently insecurity. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: The order of Honourable Members speaking during the Zero Hour concludes here. Names of Honourable Members have been registered to speak during the Special Time based on party representation. Now, I will provide time for Honourable Members to speak. First, Honourable Member Maya Prasad Sharma, for 12 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Anand Prasad Dungana.

Honourable Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
Honourable Chairperson, I have received news of a tragic accident where a bus carrying wedding guests from Pauchudi, Baitadi, to Bajhang met with an accident in Bado village, resulting in the deaths of approximately 13 people. It is reported that 45 injured individuals have been taken to various places, including the Kotila Health Post, for treatment. The deceased are 40-year-old Keshavraj Joshi, 13-year-old Ashok Raj Joshi, 35-year-old Basanta Joshi, 41-year-old Bishnu Dutt Joshi, 42-year-old Narendra Raj Joshi, 18-year-old Kishan Dutt Joshi, 27-year-old Deepak Raj Joshi, 45-year-old Kishan Dutt Joshi, 60-year-old Mohandev Bhat, Keshav Jang Bhat, 40-year-old Basanta Raj Ratala, 40-year-old Pushpa Awasthi from Baitadi, and 14-year-old Sunil Joshi. I express my heartfelt condolences to the deceased and wish a speedy recovery to the injured. Through the Honourable Chairperson, I wish to draw the government's attention to the treatment and other assistance for the injured. Honourable Chairperson, I express my heartfelt condolences on the demise of Mr. Bhojraj Bhattarai, the 97-year-old father of former Prime Minister Dr. Baburam Bhattarai. I extend deep condolences to Dr. Baburam Bhattarai, Shiva Bhattarai, former Minister Hisila Yami, and all members of the family.

Honourable Chairperson, regarding the earthquake that occurred on Kartik 17, 2080, with its epicenter in Barekot, Jajarkot district, our committee conducted an on-site inspection in Jajarkot, Rukum Paschim, and Salyan districts from Jestha 24 to 27, 2081, and submitted a report. No action has been taken on that report so far. Winter has passed, and much of the monsoon has also passed. The people there are still living in extremely difficult conditions, having to sleep under temporary shelters. Why is the reconstruction and rehabilitation delayed? The previous government provided funds in two installments for building shelters. Then the government changed. Even after the change of government, the then Honourable Prime Minister himself expressed concern, stating that a large number of people had arrived. He expressed apprehension about the reasons for such a large influx. The houses in the hills and Jajarkot are not in convenient locations; they are made of mud and stone. They are gradually decaying and becoming uninhabitable, and this situation has worsened. Despite repeated discussions, raising the issue in the house, and consulting with stakeholders, there has been no thought, concern, interest, or initiative regarding this matter. I humbly request the ministers, through the Chairperson, to address this issue quickly and resolve the problem.

This provision of DD (likely referring to a specific type of assessment or documentation) is causing many difficulties and is more focused on hindering rather than assisting reconstruction. How has this been assessed? All these aspects require deeper study. Honourable Chairperson, from Mangsir 14 to 18, 2082, we visited various districts of Sudurpashchim for study and monitoring on behalf of our committee. Discussions were held with the press in some places, and then discussions took place at various religious sites. The Mahakali Corridor remains incomplete. Considering the aspirations of the people there, from Kanchanpur to Darchula, there were desires and interests to expedite the construction of the Mahakali Corridor. Similarly, we studied issues related to archaeology. We discussed how to conserve the scattered artifacts. We also held discussions with local levels and discussed issues related to development and construction. In the East, from Push 13 to 18, 2082, we held discussions with the Koshi Province Provincial Assembly. Specifically, we met and interacted with three or four rural municipalities, including those related to Pathibhara and Arun Rural Municipality in Bhojpur. We also discussed and observed issues related to archaeology in places like Barahachhetra, Budhasubba, Dantakali, Pindeshwor Dham, Bichkhorpa, Pathibhara, and Halesi Mandir. While the aspirations and desires of the people there are diverse, the core issue is how to coordinate between the federal, provincial, and local governments. Development projects are stalled or delayed, and there is mutual blame. How can this be managed and coordinated? How can cooperation be advanced? These issues are being raised. When questions are raised in the National Assembly, our discussions indicate that the National Assembly is alive and effective, and the government is maintaining a positive outlook towards it. We are discussing here, voicing the concerns of the people, providing suggestions, advice, and directives to the government, and operating committees. Therefore, it is natural for things to gradually fall into place. The government needs to pay special attention to how things will proceed from here.

The Mid-Hill Lokmarg (Highway), which started in 2064/065, is the road connecting Simuwa Bhanjyang in the east to Jhulaghat in Baitadi. This will be very effective for the people of the Mid-Hill region and will make many things easier and faster. However, there are obstacles to its completion. The bridge connecting Rukum Paschim and Jajarkot districts, east of Ramchap, which started in 2069, has not been constructed yet. What is causing the delay? Whenever we visit and inquire, they say they will tender it, and it will start, but the tenders are not being submitted, or no one is submitting them. This has been raised many times as it is a matter of great importance.

How can this Mid-Hill Pushpal Lal Lokmarg be managed?

It seems special attention needs to be paid. The government has cut down on development projects. What is the government's job other than development and construction? If there is irregularity, it should be controlled, monitored, and action taken. When one goes beyond the law, it should be controlled. But by cutting down all its national pride projects, the country is now stalled, the entire country is stalled. The government should not think that nothing can be done after elections. Special thought must be given to this. And when we select them, we must also think. It was said that 10 cities would be built under the Mid-Hill Highway. None of those 10 cities have been built so far. If I look towards Karnali Province, from Karnali Province, it is Chaurjahari, Rukum Paschim Chaurjahari and Dailekh's Rakam, and there is Sapebagar, and in the far west, there is Patan. Looking at the east and west, none of them have started. Although some minor work has been done in Chaurjahari, no work has been done elsewhere. Therefore, it seems that attention should be paid there. Now the election is coming, it should be impartial, free from fraud, and easy to conduct peacefully. But instead of the political parties presenting their views, engaging in various types of insults and arguments, if they clearly state their own principles, their own perspective – whether it is socialism, people's democracy, or democracy – it will be easier to explain to the public. Whatever is written on Facebook, insults are made, and abuses are hurled. This will not build anything; it will lead to a complete distortion of perspective. What is the class perspective? In whose interest are we working? What is the perspective on nationality, livelihood, and social change? How are we deriving and implementing our programs, policies, and principles? What is the immediate political agenda? What is the policy of power struggle and cooperation? What is our role in coordinating people's movements and class parliamentary roles? These are all the issues. It would be appropriate to focus on these issues. Elections will not be meaningful, nor will the public easily understand them, nor will anything be achieved, solely due to shouting. Shouting at others does not make anyone, old or new, young or old, conform to the same perspective. The old can be bad, the new can be bad. It is based on perspective. It is based on thought. It is based on their thinking, understanding, and actions. The definition that the public has adopted, that everything new is good and everything old is bad, is a bad thing, born of bad intentions. If we do such things, the new will collapse today, the old will be forgotten. The grandson is good, the grandson is bad. The grandfather is good, the grandfather is bad. This is what is happening. We need to pay attention to this. Thank you. Presiding: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Vimla Ghimire. (13:29) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Anand Prasad Dungana, time 23 minutes. (13:37) After this, Honorable Member Rukmini Koirala. Honorable Mr. Anand Prasad Dungana (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, (13:38) Today I want to present some of my views on the current situation of the country. First of all, I express my condolences on the untimely demise of our National Assembly member Baldev Bohara ji and extend my deepest sympathies to his family. After that, I am speaking for the first time in this 19th session. We thought we would do well in the 18th session, but it did not end well. To be honest, let's make this session successful and move forward, and I wish it brings good results to the nation. I have already told you all. I have divided the Janji movement of the 23rd and 24th into two parts. On the 23rd, the Janji movement raised issues like good governance, corruption, and social justice. We have also spoken about corruption; we have not failed to raise it in this house. But what I have seen is that talking about corruption and good governance is not a bad thing. The issues raised by the Janji are also good, but the way they were used has, somewhere, taken this country, this nation, to a place where I don't know where. It seems to me that the Janji movement, using these children as shields, with Molotov cocktails, removing silencers, breaking prohibited areas, and going to burn the parliament, did not burn the parliament. So, what I want to say is that the issues raised by the Janji were correct, they were right, but how they were used, who used them. I keep saying, what is Molotov? What is a Molotov cocktail? If they want their country, they will fight for it there. We also struggled for democracy for a long time. We did not burn where we lived. They do not have the right to burn here. If they want to find it in their own country, they should find it in their own country. They should not seek the freedom of their own country by coming to Nepal and trying to make the land of Nepal a battlefield, trying to destroy Nepal. I say that the incident that happened now has brought the country to a state of disintegration. It is true that the government was in Singha Durbar. The government might have made mistakes. That's why they burned Singha Durbar. What did the court do? Maybe it lost someone's case. Maybe it was angry about that. Maybe it burned that too. But if the movement was against corruption, what file was in the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA)? It was a corruption file. The CIAA was strengthened by those files, and the Home Minister himself went to jail, and the special court gave the verdict of jail. Why was the CIAA targeted? Why was that issue targeted? Why was it targeted? Because the movement was not to stop good governance and corruption, but it was a movement to destroy the country. In many places in the world, the concept of old and new is being raised. What is called old? What is called new? In old nations, the nature of China was such that whoever went, their age was 78 years. Today, China is strong in its economy. In India, Manmohan Singh was how old? So, it's not about old or new here. It's not about age here. It's about honesty. It's about nationality. I see nationality as weak. In this country, for 80 years, the Nepali Congress fought for nationality and democracy. Those Nepali Congress workers were hanged. Those Nepali Congress workers were shot. Not only in this country but also in India, they shot Koirala and Tej Bahadur Amatya. Talking about democracy, talking about democracy, I remember B.P. Koirala saying, 'If I had spoken only of democracy, I would not have gained power. If I had spoken only of nationality, I would not have gained power. I raised the issues of nationality and democracy together, and that's why this situation arose. Why did the feudal lords of this country, those who received grants from the Rana regime, those who received autocratic power from the king, all these forces stood against democracy, against the people's interest? Because the Nepali Congress raised three issues together in 2007 BS: it broke the autocratic rule, the dynastic rule; it broke the rule of a single family in the country. Second, it talked about land for everyone. In 2016 BS, B.P. Koirala got a land reform bill passed by the parliament. But look at the society today; they say it was passed by King Mahendra. All these are lies, false things. They are trying to instill them in our children and achieve wrong results. And we, born into a conservative society, still go today; you cannot enter the kitchen without taking off your trousers, without taking off your dhoti. Go there; you have to sit in the kitchen of those old families in 32 Putali by taking off your dhoti. Therefore, I say that Congress tried to bring about three changes at once. For that reason, all feudal forces, all conservative societies, all those involved in corrupt economic dealings stood against Congress. Because of this, the country has reached this state. Will this country survive or not? Today, we are standing in the National Assembly, speaking about the country. We must speak about nationality and democracy. If there is no nation, there is no democracy. If there is no nation, there is federal democratic republic. If there is no nation, where will you go? Today, Sikkim... where will it lead? It will lead there. So where is democracy needed? Therefore, I want to say, I want to urge. I also want to state clearly about the nation: if this country is to be saved, the nationalist forces of this country must unite. Otherwise, we... I said at Tilganga University, who is the chief of Tilganga University? I said that to make Tilganga University pass, there is such infrastructure. After the advent of multiparty democracy, we said there should be a university in every development sector. A university was opened in the East, asked for papers, there is no land, where to open it, where is the building, where are the employees to stay? Girija Prasad Koirala was the Prime Minister. He called me and said, 'Sir, that land in Gothgaon, in 2036 BS, the wealth of the green forest, the wealth of the green forest is the wealth of Nepal, the wealth of the mountains.' That forest was sold for mountains and independence. In that forest, after asking everyone, I settled them. I did not give it in my wife's name, nor in Girija Prasad's daughter's name. I gave it in the name of the people. Today, there are universities there, but at that time, I asked 50 times to open a university. Where is the infrastructure? Where to open it? That 5 ropani, 10 ropani, 15 ropani land near Pashupati temple. So, what is happening? We are slowly seeing where this country is being taken, where it is being led. The Nepali Congress has been finished. The Nepali Congress and the democratic party, a nationalist party, have been finished. Now, efforts are being made to finish another nationalist party, UML. Balen Shah's performance in Mahottari Ward No. 3, he will definitely win there. He won from there. He will win in Kathmandu too, but why was he taken to that Japa party?

Someone has thrown it. He has not gone. Understand one thing: until national power is consolidated here, foreign powers cannot interfere. We had and have relations with our neighbors India and Nepal based on friendship and non-alignment. What is happening today? Who is doing this? Why is this happening? Tomorrow, no foreign power will save the country. We have always been called nationalist forces. We have been called national elements. For whom to bring? For whom to save? Therefore, I want to urge that the situation created by the so-called movement is not good. Singha Durbar was burned. Did the hearts of Nepalis not ache? It was burned. Hearts did not ache. Therefore, I want to say that the hand of some foreign power is behind this situation. I say this with certainty. Krishna Prasad Bhattarai, who went to the Prime Minister's residence carrying a raincoat and umbrella as you wished, came out with that umbrella and raincoat. He was a dictator. Why did his ashram have to be burned? Why was the college burned? Krishna Prasad Koirala, for whom the Ranas disowned their property and exiled him. Even when living in exile abroad, he did not accept the Rana's authority. He was exiled not for sending Nepali caps and vests from the Siraha market to the Rana's court, but for his house being burned. In Biratnagar, Ganesh Man Singh, whom even the Prime Minister did not accept as Prime Minister. He said, 'No, I am not the one, Kismat Thapa understands this. Make him the Prime Minister.' We could not live in Chakse Bari during the Panchayat era, but we could live there. We could talk about our matters there. We could discuss democracy and loktantra there. Why was Chakse Bari burned? What did Ganesh Manji do? Therefore, I understand all these situations. I have studied a lot and tried to understand. Some foreign powers have tried to destroy our country and its democracy. Therefore, we must be very vigilant and cautious. This election is very important. If the election is not held, I often say to my friends, what will happen if the election is not held? The country will go to ruin. There could be war here. It could become Afghanistan. It could become Sri Lanka. Our opposition leaders have said this. Bangladesh is happening here. Sri Lanka is happening here. He is speaking from the rostrum. It is permissible to speak from the rostrum. If he had understood that, he is the leader of the opposition. He should have sternly warned the government. Today, in that situation, what happened in Bangladesh? Mother, listen, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was killed by the army in his house in Bangladesh. In what condition is Bangladesh today? Do we want to reach the same condition tomorrow? Should we be vigilant or not? Should we explain to the Nepali people? Look at social media, whatever people want, they write. In this election, this election is being obstructed in some way. If we are not vigilant, this election will not happen. They will not let it happen. Even if they want to, they will not let it happen. The Prime Minister has said the election will happen. It will happen once. We have also expressed our views. The election will happen. To prevent it from happening, as things are appearing on social media, as you must have seen on Facebook and TikTok, those are true. The Election Commission has formed a committee to refute them. What has the Election Commission done? Yesterday, they were saying, 'Don't panic, a complaint has been received.' I will investigate the matter of rigging in this election. The Nepali Congress filed a complaint, and you made a one-sided decision, didn't you? You did it, didn't you? You called them, didn't you? You didn't call them. So, what are you doing? How are you proceeding? How is your work going? We understand. You don't need to explain to us anymore. Therefore, I want to say that in this situation, we Nepalis, who went to jail for democracy and loktantra, went to jail 40-55 years ago. Did we really go to jail to see this day? Did we have children when we went to jail? Were our mothers crying or not? Is someone trying to bring foreign soldiers to this country and settle them like the British in India? Nepal has never been a slave to any country, nor will it be. We will not allow it as long as there is blood in our veins. The situation created in the country today, if it is true, I don't think this country will survive. But we should not give up. Mr. Chairman, in Ukraine, Zelensky was a comedian. A drama was staged there. Zelensky was brought and seated. What is happening in Ukraine today? Where is Ukraine going? Who is playing games there? They are trying to create the same situation here. We should not let this become Ukraine. We should not let this monarchy reach the point of dissolution. Therefore, I want to say that if an attempt is being made to make this Ukraine, it is not a good thing. Our economy is in a very weak state. Nepal is on the grey list. To get off the grey list, look at the decision of your Attorney General. This is what the so-called movement has done. The decisions made by this Attorney General are correct. They are letting them go. Those who commit money laundering and federal crimes, 50 people each on the red notice, are also being let go. They are saying with their mouths full of arrogance that we are a cabinet that came from the so-called movement, they do not have the right to say that. Therefore, I want to urge you again. If this country is to be saved from the grey list, then those 50 people, whom you are pardoning through the Attorney General, Rabi Lamichhane, and some other person, is abroad. I remember Rabi Lamichhane was the Home Minister. He went to Chitwan and said, 'We have done what we needed to do, we have done the location, we have talked to the government, we will bring it in a few days.' He said that. That's why he ran away from there. We found out from there. That's what happened. He told the journalists. Therefore, I want to say that injustice cannot be done to the nation like this. Injustice cannot be done to the Nepali people. What is old and new justice in the world? How did the old union dissolve? Did it dissolve 50 times? We also... Someone told me the other day, 'Brother, he goes to the Terai, he goes to the mountains, he goes there. Now Karnali will not leave anyone in between. Who will not leave?' he said. So, look, let's study and reflect on all these things. We have been elected by the people. We are public representatives. We have struggled for a long time. We must think. If we don't think, if I abuse a leader of one party, and you abuse a leader of another party, and you abuse a leader of another party, and say it's nothing, and then start again, and then create a situation where we do it again, oh mother, what Oli says, oh mother, if the government comes, oh mother, if the country is lost, where will you show your face? Let's all reflect on these things. Therefore, today I want to say. The nationality of this country has weakened. The case for the restoration of parliament is pending. The judges have become so... I didn't know. Why is the Nepali judge... I know. When I was first jailed at 27, a case of fearlessness was filed. The Trade Union Control Act and Sedition. And what did the judge of that time decide? 'No, this is legislation. This is their decision. Parliament's decision. This is not sedition.' And we won the case. That also happened. It's been 45 years. Today, the judges who were so... It was the King's rule. It was the Panchayat system. Similarly, Dhanendra Bahadur Singh and... After the King did it on Poush 1, 2016, what did K.I. Singh say? 'This king has brought dictatorship.' The case against the king was filed everywhere. Now, the king appointed... Dhanendra Bahadur Singh. After Dhanendra Bahadur Singh looked at all the files, what did he write in the dismissal? 'If this is all that was said, that the king brought this on Poush 1, 2016, calling it a bit of a dictatorship. For this reason, the sedition case will not proceed.' And he went to complain to the King. 'The government brought Dhanendra Bahadur, but he did this.' 'Is that so? Is that so?' And he said, 'Yes, government.' As soon as that was said, the sedition case... What is sedition? Therefore, if not now, then we (... time expired.) Honorable Chairperson: I would like to inform the honorable member that the time has expired. (14:02 hrs) I want to inform the honorable member that the time has expired. Honorable member Rukmini Koirala, time 14 minutes, followed by honorable member Ganga Kumari Belbase. Honorable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, I have stood up to speak on the current special issues of the country during today's special time. The demands of the peaceful movement by the youth in the movement held on Bhadra 23 and 24, 082, regarding corruption, good governance, regulation of social media, opening of the internet, and making the country better, were just in themselves. However, due to infiltrators in the movement, 19 young children who came from abroad and three security personnel lost their lives. I pay my heartfelt tribute to the deceased children and security personnel. I also express my deepest condolences to the families and relatives of the deceased. On the movement of Bhadra 24, 082, wearing the national flag, carrying it, at the same time, on the same day, in the same manner, similar incidents occurred. Singha Durbar was burned, the President's residence was burned, the Supreme Court was burned, the press and local government offices were all burned, industrial establishments, public structures, and private properties were destroyed. The country was destroyed in 24 hours. Just as it was easy to break, it is also three times more difficult. Government vehicles, public and private transport vehicles, countless have been burned. Looking at the incident, it seems that plans from the past few decades have succeeded. Wearing the national flag, burning and looting computers and laptops from government offices, burning Bhatbhateni with the national flag, reaching the 7th floor wearing the national flag, and looting and stealing makeup items used by women, dolls, laptops, computers, and even fruits were seen. Private property was looted in this manner. Were those involved in theft and looting truly protestors? That is my question. All the CCTV footage is there. National property cannot be destroyed while wearing the national flag in the name of protest. The national flag has been misused. Understanding the importance of the flag, the government should take strict action, otherwise who will protect this flag? I want to say. It is heard that the government is selling the burned government vehicles and other scrap materials as scrap. However, all these burned wrecks, all these skeletons, should be kept in one place.

I want the government to preserve the history as it is and exhibit it for future generations to see, so that visitors from all over the country can come and see it through the ticket system. I want to thank Prime Minister Sushila Karki for managing the country during its difficult times. However, ministers who promised to hold elections within six months and spoke of good governance are now facing one complaint after another. This government, which has a mandate of six months, is interfering in one government institution after another. It is seen that this government is cutting short, stopping, and removing facilities for federal MPs, which were brought by the previous government, in transfers and promotions within the employee selection system. Although this government announced peaceful elections on February 21, it does not seem like that will happen. How can there be peace? Weapons looted during the movement have not been returned. Escaped prisoners have not returned. Currently, escaped prisoners are forming organizations and are organizing themselves at night. Just yesterday, they organized in Kathmandu and were looting businesses by coming on motorcycles. Just yesterday, 10 robbers were caught in Kathmandu. In Lalitpur, a husband killed his wife. Domestic violence has occurred. Therefore, the public is anxious about whether elections will be held. Who will guarantee the security of voters, ballot boxes? Who will guarantee the security of votes, polling stations, and candidates? There is doubt about whether peaceful elections will be held. Instead of holding elections, the government ministers are resigning one after another in the greed of becoming MPs and bringing in one prime minister and plunging themselves into elections. Whose advice is being followed in this country? Currently, social media has become disgusting with people verbally abusing each other, spreading obscene news, creating obscene pictures, posting obscene videos, liking and commenting with obscene words, and character assassination by attaching one person's head to another's body. This has become too much. I feel ashamed even to open my mobile. I want the government to investigate this and take swift action. Now let's talk about health. The health insurance program, which is a basic necessity for the public, provided some facilities to the people. The government's decision to close the health insurance program has left poor and needy people in uncertainty. This insurance program is very necessary. This government has snatched health insurance from the people. I want it to be managed properly and implemented again. There is the issue of cooperative victims. Their money, deposited in banks after earning by roasting corn, selling vegetables, and laboring, has been eaten by cooperative gangs, making many poor, needy, and others cry and deceive them. The government has decided to release cooperative thieves one after another, who have stolen the money of those who are struggling to eat. This decision seems to indicate that the government is trying to give impunity to the thieves. I want the government to recover the victims' money from those who have taken it and return it to the victims as soon as possible.
